question_details.description:
This question is synced with an identical question on Metaculus. The original question opened on 2024-04-30 12:30:00 and can be found [here](https://www.metaculus.com/questions/22560). This question will resolve to the same value as the synced question. The original question's background info at this time is below. 

Shortly after new Ukrainian mobilization law [was signed](https://edition.cnn.com/2024/04/16/europe/zelensky-signs-mobilization-law-intl-latam/index.html), all [consular services for men age 18-60 was suspended](https://edition.cnn.com/2024/04/23/europe/ukraine-consulates-mobilization-intl-latam/index.html), including issuing and renewing passports.

In light of these developments, there have been concerns, reportedly amplified by [Russian propaganda](https://disinfo.detector.media/en/post/the-ukrainian-government-allegedly-wants-to-cancel-the-international-passports-of-citizens-abroad), that this will be supplemented by revoking already-issued passports, thus forcing Ukrainian men to return home.

question_details.resolution_criteria:
This question will resolve as **Yes** if, before January 1, 2026, [credible sources](https://www.metaculus.com/help/faq/#definitions) report that the Ukraine government has initiated a policy of revoking previously valid passports of Ukrainian men, deemed to be of draft age, who reside outside the country.

If no credible sources report such revocation before January 1, 2026, this question resolves as **No**.

**Russia Launches Largest Autumn Draft Since 2016**
Russian President Vladimir Putin signed a decree launching a record autumn conscription campaign that will run from Oct. 1 to Dec. 31, 2025. The decree mandates the drafting of men aged 18‑30 who are not in the reserve and whose service terms have expired, and it also authorises the release of soldiers, sailors, sergeants and foremen whose contracts have ended. Federal authorities are tasked with implementing the order.

On Sept. 24, the State Duma passed a bill that will extend conscription activities throughout the calendar year, so that from Jan. 1 2026 the call‑up will no longer occur twice a year but continuously from Jan. 1 to Dec. 31. Dispatching of conscripts to service units will still occur in two periods: Apr. 1‑Jul. 15 and Oct. 1‑Dec. 31, under presidential decrees.

Moscow has denied any link between conscription and the war in Ukraine, insisting that conscripts will not be sent to the front. In contrast, Ukraine’s government has protested that thousands of the new conscripts are Ukrainian citizens who will be forced to fight against their own people.

Vice Admiral Vladimir Tsimlyanskiy, deputy chief of the Russian Army’s General Staff, told state media that in 2024 conscription was set at 130,000 men and "that goal was fulfilled on time and in full." The local outlet Novosti Rostova reported that draft summons would also be distributed through managers at state‑run companies and educational institutions. Conscripts must report to recruiting offices and are obliged to serve for twelve months.

Recruitment priorities for 2024 include the Komi Republic, Krasnodar, Krasnoyarsk, Amur, Kaliningrad, Moscow, Bryansk, Rostov, Samara, Sakhalin, St. Petersburg and Chelyabinsk regions, with Crimea described by Tsimlyanskiy as Russian territory and also listed as a key focus.

Those labeled foreigners will be subject to residency rules, including a maximum 90‑day stay, mandatory medical exams and work restrictions. Anyone forced to take a Russian passport automatically becomes eligible for conscription.
